markets_note: Stocks were mixed, with the S&P 500 down 0.47% and the Nasdaq down 0.71% while the Dow gained 0.41%. The 10 year Treasury yield sat near 4.99%, the VIX rose to 19.45, and futures pointed lower.

items.title: AM Best: Social Inflation Drives Surge in Commercial Auto Liability Claims
items.summary: An AM Best report says rising litigation costs, often called social inflation, are driving up commercial auto liability claims. First year loss payments grew about 6.4% a year from 2014 to 2024, versus 2.8% yearly economic inflation. Claims are staying open longer, which leaves more exposure to jury verdicts, and umbrella pricing has climbed as large auto claims spill into excess coverage. The report notes that Florida's tort reforms have helped bring average claim costs down.

items.title: Oklahoma Landlord to Pay $52K for Violating Fair Housing Act
items.summary: The Justice Department announced that an Oklahoma City rental property's owners will pay $52,500 to settle a Fair Housing Act suit. The suit alleged a manager refused to rent to a single mother because her young son would live there. The settlement also requires a nondiscrimination policy and training. This is a federal court matter in Oklahoma, so it is persuasive only for Missouri purposes.

items.title: New Mexico’s outside lawyers could collect up to $1.27 billion in Meta case
items.summary: Headline only, the article is paywalled and was not read. The headline reports that outside lawyers working for New Mexico could collect up to $1.27 billion in fees in a case against Meta. Nothing further is known beyond the headline, and any out of state outcome would be persuasive only in Missouri.

items.title: Dow and Small Caps Climb Weekly While Nasdaq Slips on Megacap Earnings Charges
items.summary: A press release style weekly wrap describes a volatile earnings week with a split result: the Dow and small caps rose while the Nasdaq slipped on weakness in large tech names. It reports the VIX near 19.4, the 10 year Treasury yield easing to 4.99%, gold and silver falling, and crude oil jumping on Thursday. It also notes Meta booked a large charge tied to an agreement with state attorneys general over teen social media litigation. This is promotional commentary, so treat the figures with some care.

items.title: Wells Fargo Names Top Pick Ahead of Q3 Earnings
items.summary: Wells Fargo named Amazon its top long idea among mega cap stocks heading into third quarter earnings. The bank expects Amazon Web Services to drive positive revisions to revenue and operating income. It acknowledges some near term risk from fuel costs and longer term questions about agentic commerce.

items.title: Adobe Stock Has Been Under Pressure. Here’s What Could Spark a Turnaround
items.summary: Adobe keeps beating earnings estimates, yet the stock is down about 27% this year, and the article lays out the debate over why. The writer's price target is $298.13, about 16% above the current $256.13, citing a new CEO on December 1 and fast growth in AI related revenue. Risks include a 36% to 37% drop in net new recurring revenue, a CFO exit, and 23 analysts rating it a hold.

items.title: One of the World’s Top Marathoners Has Been Provisionally Suspended After an EPO Finding
items.summary: The Athletics Integrity Unit provisionally suspended marathon star Peres Jepchirchir after an out of competition sample taken in Kenya before her Sydney Marathon win tested positive for EPO. This is not a final ruling and the case still has to go through the formal process. Under World Marathon Majors rules, a doping ban of three months or more would mean a lifetime ban from those events.

items.title: MLB Pipeline Pitching Lab: Tekoah Roby
items.summary: Cardinals prospect Tekoah Roby, back from Tommy John surgery, has allowed no runs through three Arizona Fall League starts, with 13 strikeouts and one walk over 9 and 2/3 innings. His fastball averaged 97.0 mph in his debut, though he says that was mostly adrenaline and it has settled to about 95.6 to 95.8 since. He describes the fastball mainly as a setup pitch for his breaking balls.

items.title: An Elite Marathoner Blamed a Prescription for Her Positive Doping Test. The Problem? The ‘Doctor’ Who Wrote It Wasn’t a Doctor.
items.summary: Based on the excerpt only. Elite marathoner Ruti Aga, a podium finisher at six World Marathon Majors and the 2019 Tokyo winner, blamed a prescription for a positive doping test. The headline says the problem is that the person who wrote it was not a doctor.
